authorization: Phase B runs only after explicit owner approval; results are evidence for a separate owner decision and never change production automatically

inherited_procedure.family: recursive_iid_residual (v1.86 selected by preregistered tie rule)
inherited_procedure.statistic: tau = asymptotic chi-square p-value of the adjusted Portmanteau at h=12 for the model's own lag
inherited_procedure.synthetic_gate_reference: v1.86 selected-model-adequacy gate (synthetic only; not an authorization)

pipeline: production BIC lag selection (candidate lags 1..10, common sample)
VAR estimation at the selected lag on the full effective sample
recursive iid residual bootstrap samples from the fitted VAR under the whiteness null (centred residuals, initial values = first p observations, same calendar months)
BIC re-selection inside every bootstrap sample with the same policy
re-estimation and tau* for every bootstrap sample
bootstrap p-value = (1 + #{tau*_b <= tau}) / (B + 1); decision at 0.05 reported, never applied to readiness
B_rationale: single observed series per unit, so a larger B than the synthetic study is affordable; alpha*(B+1) = 100 is an integer (Davidson and MacKinnon 2000)
month_index_mapping: engine month index = (calendar_month + 10) mod 12 so that January is the omitted dummy, as in production; the constant + 11 dummies column space is identical under any omitted month, and residual equality with production is checked to 1e-8 before bootstrapping

numerical_failure_rules.unstable_or_nonfinite_original_fit: report 'bootstrap_unavailable' with the engine state; no retry
numerical_failure_rules.nonfinite_bootstrap_statistic: report 'bootstrap_failed'; no retry, no draw replacement
numerical_failure_rules.singular_design: least-squares fallback as in the frozen engine

convergence_criterion: the bootstrap is a fixed-B Monte Carlo with no iterative solver; completion = all B statistics finite
monte_carlo_uncertainty: binomial standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/B) of the bootstrap p-value and the 99% Clopper-Pearson interval for the underlying exceedance probability; decisions whose 99% interval straddles 0.05 are labelled 'Monte Carlo borderline'

labels: not a replacement of the production diagnostic
